- The launcher no longer changes the phone's wallpaper by itself: Phone wallpaper follows the launcher is off unless you switch it on.
- Windows 10 and 11: the Win+X menu can be edited (items and order); Windows keyboard shortcuts work from a physical keyboard or Pulse's keyboard: Win+X, Win+R, Win+E, Win+I, Win+S, Win+D and the Windows key alone for Start; the search finds Control Panel, Registry Editor, Terminal, Task Manager and the other tools by name; the Control Panel is dark and see-through in Windows 11 and shows two columns when there is room. The Messages tray icon is gone again.
- Windows 7: the MSN Messenger tray icon opens Messages as a small popup at the bottom right, by the tray, instead of a big window (the Messages tray icon is only there, in the MSN years' look).
- Windows 10 and 11 Start menu: Command Prompt, Control Panel, Registry Editor, Task Manager, Services and Startup apps are in its apps list and its search.
- Launcher: windows open a notch smaller; the number on a notification badge is centred in its dot.
- Windows 11: the black of an app in a window is dark glass (the blurred desktop shows through; a switch in Look turns it off); Notes' folder panel opens inside its window, not over the whole screen.
- Launcher: every extra app of Pulse (Files, Photos, Calendar, Contacts, Code, YTXTube, Health ...) is in this launcher's apps list by default, though the phone's own launchers do not list them.
- Pulse's file picker: the kind chips (All, Pictures, Videos, Audio, Documents, Archives) have icons; the launcher opens other apps in a window of the desktop by default (Windows looks; on a phone that has no windows they open as before).
- Windows looks: the extra apps from the apps list open in windows of the desktop (Files, Photos, Health, Code, Calculator, Music, Video, Notes, Weather, Messages, Browser, Office, Paint, Clock ...); Calendar, Contacts and YTXTube keep their own screens.
- Windows looks: the drawn mouse arrow is not drawn while a mouse is connected (two pointers showed, most at a right click).
- Launcher widgets: a held widget (its controls show) has a corner at the bottom right to drag it to any size, kept for next time; in the launcher settings a tap on a placed widget's picture no longer opens what the widget opens (a web page).
- Task manager: the first column's rule runs the full height of the row (it was cut short); the row and column lines are fainter.
- Torrents: encrypted connections only (on by default; Series and movies download settings), which gets through many school and hotel Wi-Fi networks that block BitTorrent by its traffic. The launcher's quick search panel is see-through.
- Launcher: Freeform windows for other apps (Home screen settings) switches Android's freeform window settings on with the secure-settings permission (one adb command once), root or Shizuku.
- Keyboard: a physical keyboard is found more surely (a tablet's keyboard cover, a second check of the system's own report), so Pulse's keyboard shows its suggestion bar only.
- Windows 10 and 11: when Pulse is the home app, the Windows key of a keyboard (which makes the phone send the home intent) opens and closes the Start menu instead of going home.
- The phone's own wallpaper also comes back when the launcher opens while another launcher is the home app (it came back only when Pulse's main app opened).
- Windows looks' power menu: Shut down closes the launcher, Restart starts it again with the BIOS and start-up screens, Sign out shows the sign-in screen (the phone itself is not shut down or restarted).
- Keyboard: with a physical keyboard connected, a field opens as the suggestion bar at once (the connection is checked before the keyboard is drawn); the full keys come only from the bar's keyboard button and each new field starts as the bar again.
- Launcher: apps are asked for a window size only when Android's freeform windows are on (apps opened with a window size could be missing from the recent apps).
- Text widgets (weather, battery, CPU ...): on a bigger tile the number grows with it and the text block sits lower, not in the top corner of an empty tile.
- Photo frame widget: with no photo yet it is a visible tile with a picture mark and a plus (it was invisible); a tap opens the choice and editing of the photo.
- Widgets: the system, battery, storage, memory, network, clock and download text widgets are square (2x2) by default and can be resized wider.
- Add gadgets: every group of Pulse's widgets is open, each a row that slides sideways (like the Windows 11 widget board).
- Launcher wallpaper: a picture of your own for the turned phone as well as for the phone held upright (with only one chosen it serves both); the picture set as the phone's wallpaper is cut from its middle to the shape of the screen, no zoom.
- Settings > Apps: every app is a single compact row (picture, name, home-screen switch, pin, place) instead of a big tile; Good Lock and Buds manager have colour Fluent-style pictures.
- Windows 11 Settings / Control Panel: the "Open in the phone's settings" button is gone; each setting page has controls that work inside Pulse (Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, airplane, mobile data, NFC, location with Shizuku or root; Do not disturb, ringer, dark mode, rotation, screen timeout, text size, battery saver, time, keyboard picker, accessibility switches; Lock screen: lock now and lyrics on the lock screen). Control Panel items open the same pages.
- Pulse launcher: it has its own task affinity now, so Pulse (the main app) opened from it gets its own entry in Recents instead of sitting inside the home task.
- Text input page opens Pulse's own keyboard settings.
- Bluetooth & devices: the top shows the last three devices (connected ones first) as big cards and a big plus card that looks for and pairs new devices inside Pulse (no hand-off to the phone's Settings); BLUETOOTH_SCAN permission added.
- Settings pages: NFC (state, tap to pay, payment app), USB (power, connected devices), Cameras (each lens and megapixels), Location, Date & time, Language, Text input show real details of the phone.
- Pulse AI Models: the line under the title (RAM · folder) is tappable and picks the folder searched for models; by default every model on the phone is found, starting with Download (a chosen folder replaces that; ✕ goes back to the whole phone).
- Keyboard clipboard: a copy the system never reported (older than 2 minutes when the keyboard opens) is added to the clipboard list instead of being skipped; a picture whose saved file is gone no longer stays as an empty tile.
- Music: covers found online are kept at 512 px / about 50 KB instead of 600 px / 100-200 KB.
- Settings > About > Storage: the covers folder is split into Book covers and Music covers (own sizes, own Delete), and every folder opens a list of what is inside (picture, name, size).
- Physical keyboard on the Windows 10/11 launcher: Win+L lock, Win+M minimise all, Win+A quick settings, Win+Up/Down maximise/restore/minimise the front window, Alt+F4 closes it, Alt+Tab goes to the next window, Ctrl+Esc is Start, Esc closes an open menu (besides Win, Win+X/R/E/I/S/Q/D from before).
- Physical keyboard Windows key: with Pulse as the home app (Windows 10 / 11 look) and the screen cover accessibility service on, the Windows key (and Win+letter shortcuts) is taken before One UI can open its own launcher and goes to Pulse's launcher.
- Windows desktop: Win+Left/Right snap the front window to a half of the screen (drag it to a side edge, top edge = full screen), Win+Down puts it back; Win+Tab shows every window as a card (task view); a mouse right click opens the context menu on files and the desktop.
